subject.title: In-turn background work (Workflow / run_in_background / Workflow-backed skills) is SIGKILLed at the turn boundary under the claude-cli runtime

question: Should claude-cli post-turn background work be supported through an OpenClaw-owned durable lifecycle contract, or should OpenClaw continue failing closed for every unsupported background affordance on this runtime?
rationale: The evidence shows a shipped fail-closed mitigation for native Bash/Monitor but no owner-approved contract for Workflow-backed survival, origin snapshotting, and completion delivery.

options.title: Define durable lifecycle contract
options.body: Adopt an OpenClaw-owned survival plus delivery contract and keep native Claude background affordances denied until each supported path has live proof.

options.title: Fail closed and document non-support
options.body: Make claude-cli background work consistently unavailable when OpenClaw cannot own both survival and completion routing.

options.title: Split into narrower delivery/runtime issues
options.body: Keep this umbrella open only for design while tracking implementation in separate process-lifetime and delivery-queue items.

recommendation.title: Define durable lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Adopt an OpenClaw-owned survival plus delivery contract and keep native Claude background affordances denied until each supported path has live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The most central current-history signal is the warm Claude live-session implementation that owns the process lifecycle involved here.
